why:
Hand count from the evidence alone.
STEP 1 -- when the clock starts. The application was accepted as complete at 9:15 AM Monday 10 August, and the count begins on the first business day AFTER acceptance (e5), so counting starts Tuesday 11 August.
STEP 2 -- which days count. A business day counts only if no request for additional information (RAI) is outstanding at 12:00 noon that day (e6). The RAI was issued Thursday 13 August at 3:00 PM (e7) and answered completely Wednesday 26 August at 10:00 AM (e8). So it was outstanding at noon on Fri 14, Mon 17, Tue 18, Wed 19, Thu 20, Fri 21, Mon 24 and Tue 25 August, and it was NOT outstanding at noon on 13 August (issued at 3:00 PM, after noon) nor at noon on 26 August (answered at 10:00 AM, before noon). Those two boundary days therefore both count.
STEP 3 -- which days are business days at all. Weekends are excluded, and so are the two declared county closures, Monday 7 September and Friday 11 September (e3, e4).
STEP 4 -- the count. 1 = Tue 11 Aug; 2 = Wed 12 Aug; 3 = Thu 13 Aug; Fri 14 Aug through Tue 25 Aug are tolled and count for nothing; 4 = Wed 26 Aug; 5 = Thu 27 Aug; 6 = Fri 28 Aug; 7 = Mon 31 Aug; 8 = Tue 1 Sep; 9 = Wed 2 Sep; 10 = Thu 3 Sep; 11 = Fri 4 Sep; Mon 7 Sep is a county closure; 12 = Tue 8 Sep; 13 = Wed 9 Sep; 14 = Thu 10 Sep; Fri 11 Sep is a county closure; 15 = Mon 14 September 2026.
STEP 5 -- the conclusion. Deemed approval takes effect at 5:00 PM on Monday 14 September 2026 (e2), three days after the 5:00 PM Friday 11 September deadline. The department itself will issue no decision before 21 September (e9) and no one can shorten the process (e10). The application is therefore neither approved by decision nor deemed approved before the deadline. Answer: no.
NAIVE WRONG ANSWERS. (a) Counting fifteen business days straight from Tuesday 11 August while ignoring the tolling rule lands on Monday 31 August, which is before the deadline and gives 'yes'. (b) Applying the tolling correctly but forgetting the two county closures lands on Thursday 10 September at 5:00 PM, which is still before the Friday 11 September deadline and also gives 'yes'. Only a count that applies BOTH the tolling window AND both closures reaches 14 September and yields 'no'. Note the sharpest detail: 11 September, the deadline day itself, is one of the two closure days, so it cannot be the fifteenth counted day either.
